title: Proper ideals in finite function subrings admit residue evaluation tests
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative unital ring which is finitely generated as a $\mathbf Z$-module, meaning that finitely many elements of $A$ span its additive group with integer coefficients. Let $X$ be a finite nonempty set and $B\subseteq A^X$ a unital subring containing every constant function $x\mapsto a$ for $a\in A$; operations in $A^X$ are coordinatewise. For every proper ideal $I\subsetneq B$ there exist $x\in X$ and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak q\subset A$ such that $f(x)\in\mathfrak q$ for every $f\in I$. Here maximal means proper and maximal among proper ideals. Moreover $A/\mathfrak q$ is a finite nonzero field, hence has characteristic a prime $p$. Finitely generated modules have the meaning of [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; $A/\mathfrak q$ is the quotient module [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module] equipped with coset multiplication $(a+\mathfrak q)(b+\mathfrak q)=ab+\mathfrak q$. An ideal here is an additive subgroup closed under multiplication by all elements of the ambient ring; a unital subring contains $1$ and is closed under addition, additive inverses and multiplication.

source.place: Agent-written finite-product consequence of Tag 00GQ, lemma-integral-overring-surjective, and Tag 00GR, lemma-integral-under-field. The coordinate-prime identification and finite residue-field assertion are additional content, not the statement of 00GQ alone.

proof.text: Put $C=A^X$ and let $j:B\hookrightarrow C$ be inclusion. Write $c_a\in B$ for the constant function with value $a\in A$. For $g\in C$, form $P_g(T)=\prod_{x\in X}(T-c_{g(x)})\in B[T]$. Its leading coefficient is the product of the leading coefficients $1$, so it is monic. At every coordinate $y\in X$, evaluation at $g$ gives $P_g(g)(y)=\prod_{x\in X}(g(y)-g(x))=0$, because the factor indexed by $y$ is zero. Thus $P_g(g)=0$ in $C$. This proves directly that every element of $C$ is integral over $B$, meaning a root of a monic polynomial over $B$. The inclusion $j$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 00GQ, lemma-integral-overring-surjective: integrality hypothesis; explicit finite-product verification written by Q74

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] to $I\subsetneq B$ to choose a maximal ideal $M\supseteq I$. It is prime: if $ab\in M$ and $a\notin M$, maximality gives $1=u+ra$ with $u\in M$, $r\in B$, hence $b=ub+rab\in M$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] to the integral injective inclusion $j$ established in Step 1 and the prime $M$. It supplies a prime ideal $P\subset C$ with $j^{-1}(P)=M$.

source.place: Tag 00GQ, lemma-integral-overring-surjective; Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology, part (2) and proof of part (8), for a maximal ideal containing a proper ideal

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal], the prime $P$ is maximal, since $C$ is integral over $B$ and $j^{-1}(P)=M$ is maximal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-product-prime-factor] to the finite product $C=\prod_{x\in X}A$. There are $x\in X$ and a prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$ with $P=\operatorname{ev}_x^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. This $\mathfrak q$ is maximal: if $\mathfrak q\subseteq J\subsetneq A$ is an ideal, then $\operatorname{ev}_x^{-1}(J)$ is a proper ideal containing $P$, hence equals $P$. Evaluation is surjective, since $\operatorname{ev}_x(c_a)=a$, so taking images yields $J=\mathfrak q$. For every $f\in I\subseteq M=j^{-1}(P)$ we now have $f(x)\in\mathfrak q$, proving the evaluation assertion.

source.place: Tag 00GS, lemma-integral-over-field, for maximality above a maximal ideal; Tag 00ED, lemma-spec-product, iterated over the finite index set, for the coordinate prime; maximality along surjective evaluation proved explicitly

proof.text: By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-quotient-field], $K=A/\mathfrak q$ is a field. It is nonzero since $\mathfrak q$ is proper, so $1+\mathfrak q\ne0+\mathfrak q$. Choose additive generators $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ of $A$ as in [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The quotient map of [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module] is surjective and additive. Consequently every element of $K$ has the form $\sum_{t=1}^r n_t(a_t+\mathfrak q)$ with $n_t\in\mathbf Z$, and the additive group of $K$ is finitely generated.

source.place: Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology and basic notions item-characterize-maximal-ideal; the cited quotient-field Mathlib leaf; quotient generators displayed explicitly

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-finitely-generated-abelian-group-structure] to the additive group of $K$. It gives $K\simeq\mathbf Z^n\times T$ additively, where $T$ is a direct sum indexed by a finite set of groups $\mathbf Z/(p_i^{e_i})$, with $p_i$ prime and $e_i\geq0$. If $n>0$, a free-coordinate projection composed with this isomorphism gives a surjective additive map $h:K\to\mathbf Z$. When $2\cdot1_K=0$, every $z\in K$ satisfies $2z=(2\cdot1_K)z=0$; choosing $h(z)=1$ would give $0=h(2z)=2$, a contradiction in $\mathbf Z$. When $2\cdot1_K\ne0$, multiplication by $2\cdot1_K$ is surjective, since it has a multiplicative inverse in $K$. Choose $z$ with $h(z)=1$ and $w$ with $2w=z$; then $1=2h(w)$, again impossible in $\mathbf Z$. Thus $n=0$. Each $p_i^{e_i}$ is positive, including the case $e_i=0$, and each cyclic group has that finite number of residue classes. An element of $T$ is a tuple in the product of these finitely many finite sets, so $T$, and hence $K$, is finite.

source.place: AddCommGroup.equiv_free_prod_directSum_zmod, lines 119-132; elementary elimination of free coordinates using the field operations

proof.text: Since $K$ is finite, two members of the infinite list $0,1_K,2\cdot1_K,\ldots$ agree. Their difference gives a positive integer annihilating $1_K$. Let $p$ be the least such integer; it is not $1$, because $K$ is nonzero. If $p=uv$ with $1<u,v<p$, minimality says $u\cdot1_K$ and $v\cdot1_K$ are nonzero, whereas their product is $p\cdot1_K=0$. This contradicts the absence of zero divisors in a field. Thus $p$ is prime and is the characteristic of $K$, as required.

source.place: Elementary finite-field characteristic argument written by Q74
